name: Jeremiah
sourceNote: Translated from the Hebrew of the Westminster Leningrad Codex (the Masoretic Text, MT), checked against the Septuagint (LXX) through Brenton’s public-domain English translation. Jeremiah survives in two editions. The Old Greek is about one-eighth shorter than the Hebrew (commonly estimated at some 2,700 fewer words), and it arranges the book differently: the oracles against the nations (Hebrew chapters 46–51) stand in the middle of the book, after 25:13, as Greek chapters 25:14–31:44 (often cited as LXX chs. 26–51), in a different order of nations (Elam, Egypt, Babylon, Philistia, Edom, Ammon, Kedar, Damascus, Moab), and the rest of the book is renumbered. Among the Dead Sea Scrolls, two Cave 4 manuscripts (4QJer-b and 4QJer-d) are reported to agree with the shorter, LXX-type text, while 4QJer-a and 4QJer-c support the longer Masoretic edition; so both editions existed in Hebrew, and many scholars regard the shorter one as the earlier. This translation follows the Hebrew, in its order and verse numbering. Whole verses that Brenton’s Septuagint lacks are footnoted where they occur (for example 10:6–8, 10; 17:1–4; 33:14–26; 39:4–13; 52:28–30); smaller Greek minuses (repeated titles such as “says Yahweh,” “of Armies,” and doublets) are too many to list and are described in general terms. Where the Greek order differs, the note gives the Greek location as numbered in Brenton. Qumran readings are stated in general terms (“is reported to”) until checked against the critical edition. Much of Jeremiah is poetry and is printed line by line; prose narrative and sermons are printed as paragraphs. Calendar months are given with their modern equivalents and footnoted. The Hebrew name of God, YHWH, is written “Yahweh”; “Yahweh of Armies” renders YHWH Sabaoth (see the note at 2:19).

verses.text: The words of Jeremiah{a} the son of Hilkiah,{b} of the priests who were in Anathoth{c} in the land of Benjamin,
to whom the word of Yahweh came in the days of Josiah{d} the son of Amon, king of Judah, in the thirteenth year of his reign.{e}

It came also in the days of Jehoiakim{f} the son of Josiah, king of Judah, until the end of the eleventh year of Zedekiah{g} the son of Josiah, king of Judah, until the carrying away of Jerusalem into exile in the fifth month (in July–August).{h}
Now the word of Yahweh came to me, saying,

Then I said, “Ah, Lord Yahweh!{i} See, I do not know how to speak,
for I am a youth.”

Be not afraid of their faces,
for with you am I to deliver you,” declares Yahweh.

Then Yahweh put forth his hand and touched my mouth, and Yahweh said to me,
“See, I have put my words in your mouth.

See, I have set you this day over the nations and over the kingdoms,
to pluck up and to pull down,
to destroy and to overthrow,
to build and to plant.”
And the word of Yahweh came to me, saying, “What do you see, Jeremiah?” And I said, “A branch of an almond tree{j} I see.”
Then Yahweh said to me, “You have seen well, for I am watching{k} over my word to perform it.”
And the word of Yahweh came to me a second time, saying, “What do you see?” And I said, “A boiling pot I see, and its face is turned away from the north.”{l}
Then Yahweh said to me, “Out of the north disaster shall break loose upon all the inhabitants of the land.

For see, I am calling all the clans of the kingdoms of the north,” declares Yahweh, “and they shall come, and each shall set his throne at the entrance of the gates of Jerusalem, against all its walls round about, and against all the cities of Judah.
And I will speak my judgments against them for all their evil, in that they have forsaken me and have burned incense{m} to other gods and bowed down to the works of their own hands.
But you, gird up your loins; arise and speak to them all that I command you. Be not dismayed before them, lest I dismay you before them.

And I—see, I have made you this day a fortified city, and a pillar of iron, and walls of bronze against the whole land, against the kings of Judah, against its princes, against its priests, and against the people of the land.
And they will fight against you, but they shall not prevail against you, for with you am I,” declares Yahweh, “to deliver you.”

notes.text: Jeremiah (Hebrew Yirmeyahu) probably means “Yahweh exalts” or “Yahweh founds”; the meaning is uncertain.
Hilkiah means “My portion is Yahweh.”
Anathoth, a priestly town about 3 miles (5 kilometers) northeast of Jerusalem (Joshua 21:18); Abiathar the priest was banished there (1 Kings 2:26).
Josiah probably means “Yahweh supports” or “Yahweh heals”; uncertain.
That is, about 627 B.C.
Jehoiakim means “Yahweh raises up.”
Zedekiah means “Yahweh is righteousness.”
Hebrew “the fifth month,” Av, counted from the spring new year; that is, in 586 B.C. (see 52:12). The modern equivalent is approximate, since the Hebrew year was lunar.
Hebrew Adonai Yahweh. The Septuagint reads “O Lord, you that are supreme Lord” (Brenton, modernized).
Hebrew shaqed, “almond tree,” sounds like shoqed, “watching” (verse 12). The almond was called “the watcher” or “the wakeful tree” because it blossoms first in the year.
Hebrew shoqed; see the note at verse 11. The Septuagint reads “I have watched over my words to perform them” (Brenton).
Or “tilted away from the north,” that is, about to pour out toward the south.
Or “made offerings go up in smoke.”

verses.text: And the word of Yahweh came to me, saying,{a}

“Go and cry in the ears of Jerusalem, saying, ‘Thus says Yahweh:
I remember for you the devotion{b} of your youth,
the love of your bridal days,
your going after me in the wilderness,
in a land not sown.

Hear the word of Yahweh, O house of Jacob,
and all the clans of the house of Israel.

Thus has Yahweh spoken:
“What fault did your forefathers detect in me,
that far from me they strayed,
pursued what is vapor,{c} and turned to vapor?

And they did not say, ‘Where is Yahweh,
who brought us up from the land of Egypt,
who led us in the wilderness,
in a land of deserts and pits,
in a land of drought and deep darkness,
in a land through which no man passed
and where no human being dwelt?’

“Therefore I will yet contend with you,” declares Yahweh,
“and with your children’s children I will contend.

For cross over to the coasts of Kittim{g} and see,
and send to Kedar{h} and consider diligently,
and see if there has been such a thing as this.

Has a nation exchanged its gods,
even though they are no gods?
Yet my people have exchanged their glory{i}
for that which does not profit.

Be appalled, O heavens, at this;
shudder, be utterly desolate,” declares Yahweh,

“for two evils my people have committed:
me they have forsaken,
the fountain of living waters,
to hew out for themselves cisterns,
broken cisterns, which cannot hold water.

“Is Israel a bondman? Or one born in the household?
Why then has he become spoil?

Also the men of Noph{j} and Tahpanhes{k}
have grazed{l} the crown of your head.

Is not this your own doing,
in abandoning Yahweh your God
when he guided you on the road?

“For long ago you broke your yoke
and tore off your bonds,
and you said, ‘I will not serve.’
For on every high hill
and under every green tree
you sprawled as a harlot.

Yet I had planted you a choice vine,
wholly of true seed.
How then have you turned yourself into
the degenerate shoots of a foreign vine before me?

For though you wash with lye
and use for yourself much soap,
the stain of your iniquity is before me,”
declares the Lord Yahweh.

a wild donkey used to the wilderness,
in the lust of her soul sniffing the wind!
In her heat who can turn her back?
All who seek her need not weary themselves;
in her month they will find her.

Keep your foot from going unshod
and your throat from thirst.
But you said, ‘It is hopeless!
No, for I have loved strangers,
and after them I will go.’

“As a thief is shamed when he is caught,
so the house of Israel is shamed—
they, their kings, their princes,
their priests, and their prophets—

who say to a tree, ‘You are my father,’
and to a stone, ‘You gave birth to me.’
For they have turned to me their back, and not their face;
but in the time of their trouble they say,
‘Arise and save us!’

“Why do you contend with me?
All of you have transgressed against me,” declares Yahweh.

“To no purpose I smote your sons;
correction they would not receive.
Your sword consumed your prophets
like a ravaging lion.

Can a virgin forget her ornaments,
or a bride her sash?
Yet my people have forgotten me
days without number.

“How well you direct your way to seek love!
Therefore even the wicked women
you have taught your ways.

you say, ‘I am innocent;
surely his anger has turned from me.’
See, I will enter into judgment with you
because you say, ‘I have not sinned.’

How lightly you go about,
changing your way!
By Egypt also you shall be put to shame,
as you were put to shame by Assyria.

notes.text: The Septuagint lacks verse 1 and the opening words of verse 2, reading simply “And he said, Thus says the Lord” (Brenton, modernized).
Hebrew ḥesed, loyal love or covenant faithfulness.
Hebrew hevel, “vapor” or “breath,” often used of idols; the verb that follows plays on it.
Hebrew “a land of the Carmel,” that is, a garden land.
That is, the rulers.
Baal, “lord” or “master,” the Canaanite storm god.
Kittim, originally Kition on Cyprus; here the western islands and coastlands generally.
Kedar, a tribe of the Arabian desert to the east; so the verse means “search from west to east.”
An ancient Jewish tradition counts this as one of the “corrections of the scribes,” the original reading being “my glory.”
Noph is Memphis, the ancient capital of Lower Egypt.
Tahpanhes, an Egyptian frontier fortress in the eastern Nile Delta; see 43:7–9.
Or “have shaved” or “have broken”; the Hebrew is uncertain.
Shihor, a branch of the Nile, or the Nile itself; the Septuagint has “Geon” (Brenton).
That is, the Euphrates.

Hebrew Adonai YHWH Tsevaʾot. “Yahweh of Armies” (traditionally “the LORD of hosts”) presents God as commander of the heavenly armies and of Israel’s forces. This title occurs more than 80 times in the Hebrew of Jeremiah; the Septuagint very often lacks “of Armies,” and here reads “says the Lord your God” (Brenton, modernized).
Probably the Valley of Ben-hinnom (see 7:31); the Septuagint reads “the burial-ground” (Brenton).
The Septuagint adds, “and according to the number of the streets of Jerusalem they sacrificed to Baal” (Brenton); compare 11:13.
Or “a land of deep gloom,” Hebrew maʾpelyah, found only here.
That is, they were not burglars caught in the act, whom it would have been lawful to kill (Exodus 22:2).
A gesture of grief and shame (2 Samuel 13:19).

verses.text:
“If a man sends away his wife,{a}
and she goes from him
and becomes another man’s,
will he return to her again?
Would not that land be greatly polluted?
But you have played the harlot with many lovers;
and would you return to me?” declares Yahweh.

“Lift up your eyes to the bare heights{b} and see:
where have you not been lain with?
Beside the roads you have sat waiting for them,
like an Arab{c} in the wilderness,
and you have polluted the land
with your harlotries and your wickedness.

Therefore the showers have been withheld,
and the spring rain{d} has not come.
Yet the forehead of a harlot woman was yours;
you refused to be ashamed.

Have you not just now cried to me,
‘My father, the companion of my youth are you!

Will he keep his anger forever?
Will he guard it to the end?’
See, so you have spoken,
yet you have done all the evil that you could.”
And Yahweh said to me in the days of Josiah the king, “Have you seen what she did, faithless Israel?{e} She went up on every high mountain and under every green tree, and there played the harlot.
And I said, after she had done all these things, ‘To me she will return’; but she did not return. And her treacherous sister Judah saw it.

And I saw that, because faithless Israel had committed adultery, I had dismissed her and handed her a writ of divorce; yet Judah her treacherous sister felt no fear, but went off and played the harlot as well.
And through the lightness of her harlotry she polluted the land, committing adultery with stone and with tree.
And yet for all this her treacherous sister Judah did not return to me with her whole heart, but in falsehood,” declares Yahweh.
Then Yahweh said to me, “Faithless Israel has shown herself more righteous than treacherous Judah.

Only acknowledge your iniquity,
that against Yahweh your God you have transgressed,
and have scattered your ways to strangers
under every green tree,
and my voice you have not obeyed,’ declares Yahweh.
Return, O faithless children,” declares Yahweh, “for I am your husband;{f} and I will take you, one from a city and two from a clan, and I will bring you to Zion.
And I will grant you shepherds suited to my heart, who will pasture you with knowledge and insight.

And when you have increased and borne fruit in the land, in those days,” declares Yahweh, “men will speak no more of ‘the ark of Yahweh’s covenant.’ It will not rise in the mind; they will neither recall it nor miss it, nor will another be made.

At that time they shall call Jerusalem ‘The Throne of Yahweh,’ and all the nations shall be gathered to it, to the name of Yahweh, to Jerusalem; and they shall walk no more after the stubbornness of their evil heart.
In those days Judah’s house shall walk alongside Israel’s house, and together they shall come out of the northern land into the land that I bestowed on your fathers as a possession.

“And I had thought,
‘How gladly would I place you with my sons,
and grant you a delightful land,
the loveliest inheritance among the nations!’
And I thought you would call me ‘My Father,’
and never turn back from following me.

Surely, as a wife treacherously leaves her companion,
so have you dealt treacherously with me, O house of Israel,” declares Yahweh.

On the bare heights a cry is heard,
Israel’s sons weeping and entreating,
for they have twisted their way;
Yahweh their God they have forgotten.

“Return, O faithless sons;
I will heal your faithlessness.”
“See, we have come to you,
for you are Yahweh our God.

Truly, a delusion are the hills,
the tumult on the mountains;
truly in Yahweh our God
is the salvation of Israel.

But the shameful thing{g} has devoured
the labor of our fathers from our youth,
their flocks and their herds,
their sons and their daughters.

notes.text: Hebrew begins “Saying,” perhaps a fragment of a lost introduction. The law of Deuteronomy 24:1–4 forbids a man to take back a divorced wife who has married another.
Hebrew shefayim, bare hills, places of pagan worship; also in verse 21.
That is, a desert nomad lying in wait to rob travelers.
Hebrew malqosh, the spring rain of March–April that ripens the grain.
Hebrew meshuvah yisraʾel, literally “turning-away Israel,” the northern kingdom, exiled by Assyria in 722 B.C. Jeremiah plays repeatedly on shuv, “turn, return” (verses 12, 14, 22).
Or “I am your master”; Hebrew baʿalti, a play on Baal.
Hebrew habbosheth, “the Shame,” a contemptuous substitute for Baal (compare 11:13).

verses.text:
“If you return, O Israel,” declares Yahweh,
“to me you should return.
If you put away your abominations from before me,
and do not waver,

and if you swear, ‘As Yahweh lives,’
in truth, in justice, and in righteousness,
then nations shall bless themselves in him,
and in him shall they glory.”

For thus says Yahweh to the men of Judah and to Jerusalem:
“Break up your fallow ground,
and do not sow among thorns.

Circumcise yourselves to Yahweh;
remove the foreskins of your hearts,
O men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem,
lest my wrath go forth like fire
and burn with none to quench it,
because of the evil of your deeds.”

Declare in Judah, and in Jerusalem proclaim, and say,
“Blow the ram’s horn in the land;
cry aloud and say,
‘Assemble, and let us go
into the fortified cities!’

For this gird on sackcloth;
lament and wail,
for the fierce anger of Yahweh
has not turned back from us.”
“And it shall come to pass in that day,” declares Yahweh, “that the heart of the king shall fail, and the heart of the princes; the priests shall be appalled, and the prophets astounded.”
Then I said, “Ah, Lord Yahweh! Surely you have utterly deceived this people and Jerusalem, saying, ‘Peace shall be yours,’ whereas the sword has reached to the very life.”{a}

At that time it shall be said to this people and to Jerusalem,
“A scorching wind from the bare heights in the wilderness
comes toward the daughter of my people,
not to winnow nor to cleanse,

a wind too strong for these comes at my bidding.
Now I also will speak judgments against them.”

See, like clouds he comes up,
and like the whirlwind his chariots;
swifter than eagles are his horses.
Woe to us, for we are ruined!

Wash your heart from wickedness, O Jerusalem,
that you may be saved.
How long shall your wicked thoughts
lodge within you?

For hark, one tells it from Dan,
and announces evil from the hills of Ephraim:{b}

“Warn the nations, see!
Proclaim against Jerusalem:
besiegers{c} come from a distant land;
they lift their voice against the cities of Judah.

Like keepers of a field they are against her round about,
because against me she has rebelled,” declares Yahweh.

“Your way and your deeds
have brought these things upon you.
This is your evil; how bitter it is!
How it reaches to your heart!”

Disaster upon disaster is proclaimed,
for the whole land is laid waste.
Suddenly my tents are laid waste,
in a moment my curtains.

How long must I see the signal
and hear the sound of the ram’s horn?

“For my people are foolish;
me they do not know.
Senseless children are they,
and they have no understanding.
Wise are they to do evil,
but to do good they know not.”

I looked on the earth, and see, it was formless and void;{e}
and to the heavens, and their light was gone.

I looked on the mountains, and see, they were quaking,
and all the hills moved to and fro.

I looked, and see, there was no man,
and all the birds of the heavens had fled.

I looked, and see, the garden land{f} was a wilderness,
and all its cities were broken down
before Yahweh, before his fierce anger.

And you, O desolate one, what will you do?
Though you clothe yourself in scarlet,
though you adorn yourself with ornaments of gold,
though you enlarge your eyes with paint,{g}
in vain you make yourself beautiful.
Your lovers despise you;
they seek your life.

For I hear a cry as of one in travail,
distress as of one bringing forth her firstborn,
the cry of Zion’s daughter, panting,
spreading her hands:
“Ah me! My life is failing
before the slayers.”

notes.text: The Septuagint reads “And I said, O sovereign Lord, truly you have greatly deceived this people” (Brenton, modernized); some ancient witnesses read “And they shall say,” making the words those of the priests and prophets.
Dan is at the far north of the land; the hill country of Ephraim lies just north of Jerusalem: the invader draws nearer.
Hebrew notsrim, “watchers” or “besiegers”; a slight change of vowels gives “enemies.”
Hebrew “My inward parts,” regarded as the seat of the emotions.
Hebrew tohu wavohu, the words of Genesis 1:2.
Hebrew “the Carmel,” the fruitful land.
Hebrew puk, a black eye-paint made of antimony or galena.

verses.text:
Run to and fro through Jerusalem’s streets,
and look, I pray, and take note;
search through her open squares,
whether you can find a man,
whether there is one who does justice,
who seeks faithfulness,
that I may pardon her.

Though they say, “As Yahweh lives,”
yet falsely do they swear.

“Why should I pardon you for this?
Your sons have forsaken me
and sworn by what are no gods.
When I fed them to the full, they committed adultery
and trooped to the harlot’s house.

Well-fed stallions, lusty,{a} they have become;
each neighs after his neighbor’s wife.

“Go up among her terraced vines and ruin them,
yet do not finish her off;
lop away her tendrils,
for they belong not to Yahweh.

For utterly faithless to me have they been,
the house of Israel and the house of Judah,” declares Yahweh.

They have lied about Yahweh
and said, “It is not he;{b}
no harm shall come upon us,
nor shall we see sword or famine.

Therefore thus says Yahweh, the God of Armies:
“Because you have spoken this word,
see, I am making my words in your mouth a fire,
and this people wood, and it shall consume them.

See, I am bringing upon you a nation from afar, O house of Israel,” declares Yahweh.
“It is an enduring nation;
it is an ancient nation,
a nation whose tongue you know not,
nor can you understand what they say.

Their quiver is a gaping tomb;
warriors, every one of them.{c}
“Yet even in those days,” declares Yahweh, “I will not make a full end of you.

And when they say, ‘For what reason has Yahweh our God done all these things to us?’ you shall say to them, ‘Just as you abandoned me and served foreign gods in your own land, so shall you serve strangers in a land not your own.’

“Announce this among Jacob’s house;
make it heard in Judah, and say:

‘Hear now this, O foolish and heartless people,
who have eyes, yet see not,
who have ears, yet hear not.

But this people has a heart both obstinate and defiant;
they have veered off and departed.

Never do they say within themselves,
“Come, let us fear Yahweh our God,
who sends rain at its proper time,
the early and the later showers,{d}
who guards for our sake
the fixed weeks of reaping.”

Your iniquities have turned these away,
and your sins have withheld the good from you.

“A horrible and appalling thing
has come to pass in the land:

the prophets prophesy falsely,
and the priests rule at their direction;{f}
and my people love it so.
But what will you do at its end?”

notes.text: Hebrew meshakim, of uncertain meaning; perhaps “well-equipped” or “lusty.”
Or “He will do nothing.”
The Septuagint lacks “Their quiver is like an open grave,” reading only “They are all mighty men” (Brenton, modernized).
Hebrew yoreh, the autumn rain (October–November), and malqosh, the spring rain (March–April).
The Hebrew of this line is uncertain.
Or “rule by their own authority”; Hebrew “by their hands.”

verses.text:
“Flee for safety, O sons of Benjamin,
out of the midst of Jerusalem!
In Tekoa{a} blow the ram’s horn,
and over Beth-haccherem{b} raise a signal,
for disaster looms out of the north,
and great destruction.

The comely and delicate one,
the daughter of Zion, I will destroy.{c}

‘Consecrate war against her!{d}
Arise, and let us go up at noon!
Woe to us, for the day declines,
for the shadows of evening stretch out!

Arise, and let us go up by night
and destroy her palaces!’”

Be warned, O Jerusalem,
lest my soul be torn from you,
lest I make you a desolation,
a land uninhabited.”

Thus says Yahweh of Armies:
“They shall glean thoroughly as a vine
the remnant of Israel;
pass your hand again, like a grape gatherer,
over the branches.”

To whom shall I speak and give warning,
that they may hear?
See, their ear is uncircumcised,
and they cannot hearken.
See, the word of Yahweh has become to them a reproach;
they take no delight in it.

Their houses shall pass over to others,
fields and wives together,
for I will stretch out my hand
against the inhabitants of the land,” declares Yahweh.

“For from the least of them to the greatest of them,
every one is greedy for unjust gain;
and from prophet to priest,
every one deals falsely.

The fracture of my people they have patched up carelessly,
declaring, ‘All is well, all is well,’
when nothing is well.

Thus has Yahweh spoken:
“Halt at the crossroads and look about;
inquire about the age-old tracks,
which is the good road, and travel on it,
and you will find repose for your souls.
But they replied, ‘We refuse to travel it.’

I set watchmen over you, saying,
‘Hearken to the sound of the ram’s horn!’
But they said, ‘We will not hearken.’

Therefore hear, O nations,
and know, O congregation, what is among them.{e}

Hear, O earth:
see, I am bringing disaster upon this people,
the fruit of their schemes,
because to my words they have not hearkened,
and my law—they have rejected it.

What use to me is incense arriving from Sheba,
or fragrant cane{f} from a far country?
Your whole offerings win no favor,
and your sacrifices give me no pleasure.”

Therefore thus says Yahweh:
“See, I am laying before this people stumbling blocks,
and fathers and sons together shall stumble on them;
neighbor and friend shall perish.”

Daughter of my people, wrap yourself in sackcloth
and wallow in the ashes;
mourn as one mourns an only son,
a wailing most bitter,
for in an instant the ravager
will fall upon us.

“I have made you an assayer and a tester{h} among my people,
that you may know and assay their way.

Rejected silver they are called,
for Yahweh has rejected them.”

notes.text: Tekoa, a town about 10 miles (16 kilometers) south of Jerusalem; its name sounds like the verb “blow” (tiqʿu).
Beth-haccherem, “house of the vineyard,” probably Ramat Rahel, between Jerusalem and Bethlehem.
Or “The daughter of Zion is like a lovely pasture”; the Hebrew is uncertain.
Warfare was begun with religious rites.
The Hebrew of this line is obscure.
Hebrew qaneh, an aromatic reed, perhaps calamus.
Hebrew magor missaviv, a favorite phrase of Jeremiah (20:3, 10; 46:5; 49:29).
Or “a fortress”; Hebrew mivtsar, perhaps a scribal note. The image is of refining silver from ore, using lead to carry off impurities.
So the Hebrew consonants read as “by fire the lead is consumed” (qere); the written text (ketiv) may be read “by their fire.”

verses.text: The word that came to Jeremiah from Yahweh, saying:{a}
“Take your stand in the gate of Yahweh’s house, and proclaim there this word, and say, ‘Hear the word of Yahweh, all you of Judah who enter these gates to bow down before Yahweh.
This is what Yahweh of Armies, Israel’s God, says: Reform your conduct and your actions, and I will let you dwell{b} in this place.
Put not your trust in lying words, saying, “The temple of Yahweh, the temple of Yahweh, the temple of Yahweh are these!”{c}
For only if you thoroughly reform your conduct and your actions, if you deal out true justice between one man and another,
if the sojourner, the fatherless, and the widow you do not oppress, and innocent blood you do not shed in this place, and after other gods you do not walk to your own harm,
then I will let you dwell in this place, in the land that I gave to your fathers from of old even for evermore.
“‘See, you are trusting in lying words that cannot profit.
Will you steal, murder, commit adultery, swear falsely, burn incense to Baal, and walk after other gods whom you have not known,
and then come and stand before me in this house, which is called by my name, and say, “We are delivered!”—only to go on doing all these abominations?
Has this house, which is called by my name, become a den of robbers in your eyes? I too, see, I have seen it,’ declares Yahweh.
“‘For go now to my place that was in Shiloh,{d} where I made my name dwell at the first, and see what I did to it because of the wickedness of my people Israel.
And now, because you have done all these deeds,’ declares Yahweh, ‘and I spoke to you, rising early and speaking, yet you did not hear, and I called you, yet you did not answer,
therefore I will do to the house that is called by my name, in which you trust, and to the place that I gave to you and to your fathers, as I did to Shiloh.
And I will cast you out from my sight, as I cast out all your brothers, the whole offspring of Ephraim.’
“As for you, do not pray for this people, nor lift up a cry or a prayer for them, nor intercede with me, for I will not hear you.
Do you not see what they are doing in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?
Sons collect sticks, fathers light the fire, and wives work the dough, to bake cakes for the Queen of Heaven;{e} and they pour libations to other gods to stir up my anger.
Is it I whom they provoke?” declares Yahweh. “Is it not themselves, to the shame of their own faces?”

Therefore thus says the Lord Yahweh: “See, my anger and my wrath will be poured out on this place, upon man and upon beast, upon the trees of the field and upon the fruit of the ground; it will burn and not be quenched.”
Thus says Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel: “Add your burnt offerings to your sacrifices, and eat flesh.{f}
For I did not speak to your fathers, nor command them, in the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt, concerning burnt offerings and sacrifices.
But this thing I commanded them: ‘Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and you shall be my people; and walk in all the way that I command you, that it may be well with you.’
But they did not obey or incline their ear, but walked in their own counsels, in the stubbornness of their evil heart, and went backward and not forward.
From the day that your fathers came out of the land of Egypt until this day, I have sent to you all my servants the prophets, daily rising early and sending them.
Still they paid me no heed and bent no ear, but hardened their necks; they behaved worse than their ancestors.
“So you shall speak all these words to them, but they will not listen to you; and you shall call to them, but they will not answer you.{g}
And you shall say to them, ‘This is the nation that did not obey the voice of Yahweh its God and did not accept correction; faithfulness has perished; it is cut off from their mouth.’

“Shear off your hair{h} and cast it away;
raise a lament on the bare heights,
for Yahweh has rejected and forsaken
the generation of his wrath.”
“For Judah’s sons have done what is evil before me,” declares Yahweh. “Their loathsome idols they have placed in the house that bears my name, and so defiled it.
And they have built the high places of Topheth,{i} which is in the Valley of Ben-hinnom,{j} to burn their sons and their daughters in the fire, which I did not command, nor did it come into my mind.

Therefore, mark this: days are approaching,” declares Yahweh, “when it will no longer be named Topheth or the Valley of Ben-hinnom, but the Valley of Killing; for they will bury in Topheth till no space is left.
And the corpses of this people will be food for the birds of the heavens and for the beasts of the earth, and none will frighten them away.

And I will make to cease from the cities of Judah and from the streets of Jerusalem the voice of mirth and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, for the land shall become a ruin.

notes.text: The Septuagint lacks verse 1 and the first half of verse 2; its text begins, “Hear the word of the Lord, all Judea” (Brenton). The same sermon is summarized in chapter 26.
Or, with a change of vowels, “and I will dwell with you”; so also in verse 7.
The Septuagint has the phrase twice: “It is the temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord” (Brenton).
Shiloh, where the tabernacle stood in the days of Eli (1 Samuel 1–4), was evidently destroyed after the Philistines captured the ark.
Probably Ishtar (Astarte), the Mesopotamian goddess of love and war, worshiped as “Queen of Heaven”; see also 44:17–25. The Septuagint reads “to make cakes to the host of heaven” (Brenton).
That is, eat even the burnt offerings, which were wholly burned; Yahweh no longer values them.
The Septuagint lacks this verse except for its opening words: “Therefore you shall speak this word to them” (Brenton, modernized).
Hebrew “your crown” (nezer), as a sign of mourning; the word is addressed to Jerusalem as a woman.
Topheth, the place in the valley where children were burned as offerings; the name may mean “fireplace,” with its vowels perhaps changed to suggest boshet, “shame.”
Ben-hinnom, “son of Hinnom,” the valley south and west of Jerusalem; its later name Gehinnom gave rise to “Gehenna.”

verses.text: “At that time,” declares Yahweh, “they shall bring out the bones of the kings of Judah, the bones of its princes, the bones of the priests, the bones of the prophets, and the bones of the inhabitants of Jerusalem out of their tombs;

and they shall spread them before the sun and the moon and all the host of the heavens, which they have loved and served, and after which they have walked, and which they have sought and worshiped. They shall not be gathered or buried; they shall be dung on the face of the ground.
And death shall be chosen rather than life by all the remnant that remains of this evil family, in all the places where I have driven them,” declares Yahweh of Armies.

“Tell them this also, ‘This is what Yahweh says:
Does a man who falls not get up?
Does one who strays not come back?

Why then has this people turned away,
Jerusalem, in a perpetual turning away?
They hold fast to deceit;
they refuse to return.

I listened and heard,
but they do not speak what is right;
no man repents of his evil,
saying, “What have I done?”
Each one turns to his own course,
like a horse plunging into battle.

Even the stork in the heavens
knows her appointed seasons,
and the turtledove, the swift,{a} and the crane
keep the time of their coming;
but my people know not
the judgment of Yahweh.

“‘How can you say, “We are wise,
and the law of Yahweh is with us”?
But see, the lying pen of the scribes
has made it into a lie.

We looked for peace, but no good came;
for a time of healing, but see, terror.

The snorting of his horses is heard from Dan;
at the noise of his chargers’ neighing
all the land trembles.
They arrive and eat up the land and everything in it,
the town and its people.

“For look, I am letting loose snakes among you,
vipers against which no charm avails,
and they will bite you,” declares Yahweh.

Past all cure is my sorrow;{f}
faint within me is my heart.

Listen, the cry of the daughter of my people
from a land far and wide:
“Is Yahweh not in Zion?
Is her King not in her?”
“Why have they provoked me to anger with their carved images,
with foreign vanities?”

“The harvest is past, the summer is ended,
and we are not saved.”

For the wound of the daughter of my people I am wounded;
I mourn; dismay has taken hold of me.

Is there no balm{g} in Gilead?
Is there no physician there?
Why then has the healing of the daughter of my people
not gone up?{h}

notes.text: The identification of these birds is uncertain; Hebrew sus or sis may be the swift or the swallow.
The Septuagint lacks verses 11–12 (Brenton), which repeat 6:14–15.
Or “I will make an end of them”; the Hebrew is uncertain.
The Hebrew of this line is obscure; the Septuagint lacks it (Brenton).
Hebrew “water of rosh,” a poisonous plant, perhaps hemlock or poppy.
The Hebrew of this line is uncertain.
Hebrew tsori, an aromatic resin used as medicine, for which Gilead, east of the Jordan, was famous (Genesis 37:25). The plant is uncertain; suggestions include mastic and the balsam tree.
That is, the new flesh has not grown over the wound. In Hebrew, 9:1 is numbered 8:23.

verses.text:
Oh that my head were waters,
and my eyes a fountain of tears,
that I might weep day and night
for the slain of the daughter of my people!{a}

Oh that I had in the wilderness
a lodging place for wayfarers,
that I might leave my people
and go away from them!
For they are all adulterers,
a company of traitors.

Your dwelling is in the midst of deceit;
through deceit they refuse to know me, declares Yahweh.

Therefore thus says Yahweh of Armies:
“See, I will refine them and test them,
for what else can I do, because of the daughter of my people?

Shall I not punish them for these things?” declares Yahweh,
“and on a nation such as this
shall my soul not take vengeance?”

“Jerusalem I will turn into rubble heaps,
a haunt of jackals,
and Judah’s towns into a waste
where no one lives.”
What man is wise enough to grasp this? To whom has Yahweh’s mouth spoken, so that he can explain it? For what cause has the land perished, scorched like the desert, with none passing through?
And Yahweh said, “Because they have forsaken my law that I set before them, and have not obeyed my voice or walked in it,
but have walked after the stubbornness of their own hearts and after the Baals, as their fathers taught them.
Therefore thus says Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel: See, I will feed this people with wormwood, and give them poisoned water to drink.
I will scatter them among the nations whom neither they nor their fathers have known, and I will send the sword after them, until I have consumed them.”

For a sound of wailing is heard from Zion:
‘How we are ruined!
We are utterly ashamed,
because we have left the land,
because they have cast down our dwellings.’”

Hear, O women, the word of Yahweh,
and let your ear receive the word of his mouth;
teach your daughters a lament,
and each her neighbor a dirge.

For death has climbed in through our windows;
it has come into our strongholds,
cutting down the little ones in the street
and the youths in the public squares.

Say this: “So declares Yahweh:
‘Human corpses will lie
like manure across the open field,
like swaths of grain behind the harvester,
with no one to gather them up.’”

This is what Yahweh says:
“The sage must not glory in his wisdom,
nor the strong man glory in his strength,
nor the wealthy man glory in his wealth;

rather, if anyone would glory, let him glory in this:
that he has insight and knows me,
that I am Yahweh, who acts with steadfast love,
with justice and with righteousness on the earth.
For in these I take pleasure,” declares Yahweh.
“See, days are coming,” declares Yahweh, “when I will punish all those who are circumcised merely in the flesh:

Egypt, Judah, Edom, the sons of Ammon, Moab, and all who clip the corners of their hair,{c} who dwell in the wilderness; for all these nations are uncircumcised, and all the house of Israel is uncircumcised in heart.”

notes.text: In Hebrew, verse 1 is numbered 8:23, and verses 2–26 are numbered 9:1–25.
Hebrew ʿaqov yaʿqov, “supplanting he supplants,” a play on the name Jacob (Genesis 27:36).
Or “who dwell in the desert with clipped temples,” a custom of certain Arab tribes; compare Leviticus 19:27.

verses.text: Hear the word that Yahweh speaks to you, O house of Israel.

Thus says Yahweh:
“Learn not the way of the nations,
nor be dismayed at the signs of the heavens,
because the nations are dismayed at them;

for the practices of the peoples are mere vapor.
Someone fells a tree in the woods,
and a carver shapes it with his chisel.

There is none like you, O Yahweh;{b}
you are great, and your name is great in might.

Who could fail to fear you, King of the nations?
For to you it rightly belongs;
for among all the sages of the nations
and throughout their realms
none can compare with you.

They are altogether stupid and foolish;
the instruction of idols is but wood.

But Yahweh is God in truth;
he is the living God, the King for all ages.
When he is angry the earth shakes,
and the nations cannot withstand his fury.
This is what you are to tell them:{d} “The gods that never made heaven and earth will vanish from the earth and from beneath these skies.”

At the sound of his voice the waters in the skies roar,
and he lifts the clouds from the far edges of the earth.
He fashions lightning to go with the rain,
and draws the wind out of his treasuries.

They are vapor, a work of mockery;
in the time of their punishment they shall perish.

Pick up your pack from the ground,
you who live under siege!

For thus says Yahweh:
“See, I am slinging out the inhabitants of the land
at this time,
and I will bring distress on them,
that they may feel it.”{f}

Woe is me because of my hurt!
My wound is grievous.
But I said, “Truly this is an affliction,
and I must bear it.”

For the shepherds are stupid
and do not inquire of Yahweh;
therefore they have not prospered,
and all their flock is scattered.

Listen, a rumor! See, it comes—
a great commotion out of the north country,
to make the cities of Judah a desolation,
a lair of jackals.

I know, O Yahweh, that the way of man is not in himself;
it is not in man who walks to direct his steps.

Correct me, O Yahweh, but in just measure;
not in your anger, lest you bring me to nothing.

Empty your fury on the nations that do not acknowledge you,
and on the clans that never invoke your name,
for they have eaten up Jacob;
they have eaten him and finished him off,
and made his pasture a waste.

notes.text: The Septuagint arranges verses 5 and 9 differently, placing the substance of verse 9 within verse 5.
The Septuagint lacks verses 6–8 and 10 (Brenton). A Hebrew manuscript from Qumran (4QJer-b) is reported to share this shorter form of the chapter.
Uphaz, an unknown place; some ancient witnesses read Ophir.
Verse 11 is in Aramaic, the only Aramaic verse in Jeremiah, and it contains a wordplay: the gods who did not “make” (ʿavadu) the heavens shall “perish” (yevadu).
That is, Yahweh, the one who belongs to Jacob as his share.
Or “that they may be found”; the Hebrew is uncertain.

verses.text: This is the word that came to Jeremiah from Yahweh:
“Hear the terms of this covenant, and speak them to Judah’s men and to Jerusalem’s residents.
Tell them, ‘This is what Yahweh, Israel’s God, says: Cursed is the man who does not heed the terms of this covenant,

which I laid upon your fathers on the day I brought them out of Egypt, out of the iron-smelting furnace, saying: Listen to my voice and carry out all that I command you. So you will be my people, and I will be your God,
that I may keep the oath I swore to your fathers, to give them a land flowing with milk and honey, as it is at this day.’” Then I answered, “Amen,{a} Yahweh.”
And Yahweh told me, “Proclaim all these words in Judah’s towns and Jerusalem’s streets: ‘Hear the terms of this covenant and carry them out.
For I solemnly warned your fathers from the day I brought them up out of Egypt down to this day, warning them early and late, saying, Listen to my voice.{b}

Yet they would not listen or turn their ear, but each walked in the obstinacy of his evil heart. So I brought upon them all the terms of this covenant, which I had charged them to keep, and which they did not keep.’”
Then Yahweh said to me, “A conspiracy has been uncovered among Judah’s men and Jerusalem’s residents.

They have gone back to the guilt of their forefathers, who would not hear my words; they too have gone after other gods to serve them. Israel’s house and Judah’s house have broken my covenant that I cut with their fathers.
Therefore this is what Yahweh says: Look, I am bringing on them a calamity they cannot escape; they will cry to me, but I will not listen.
Then Judah’s towns and Jerusalem’s residents will go and cry to the gods to whom they burn offerings, but those gods will give them no rescue whatever in the hour of their calamity.
Indeed, O Judah, your gods number as many as your towns, and the altars you have erected to the Shame{c} number as many as Jerusalem’s streets—altars for sending up smoke to Baal.
“And you—intercede not for this people; raise no plea or entreaty for them, for I will refuse to listen at the time they call on me in their calamity.

What right has my beloved in my house,
when she has worked out her many schemes?
Can vows{d} and holy flesh
take your calamity from you?
Then you could exult.

‘A leafy olive tree, lovely with goodly fruit,’
Yahweh once named you.
With the roar of a great tempest
he has set fire to it,
and its boughs are broken.{e}
Yahweh of Armies, who planted you, has pronounced calamity against you, because of the evil that Israel’s house and Judah’s house have done, provoking me by burning offerings to Baal.”

Yahweh disclosed it to me, and so I learned of it;
then you let me see what they were doing.

But you, Yahweh of Armies, who judge rightly,
who test the inmost parts{g} and the heart,
let me see your vengeance upon them,
for to you I have laid bare my cause.
Therefore this is what Yahweh says concerning the men of Anathoth, who seek your life and say, “Do not prophesy in Yahweh’s name, or you will die by our hand”—
therefore this is what Yahweh of Armies says: “See, I will call them to account. Their young men will die by the sword; their sons and daughters will die by famine.
Not a remnant will be left to them, for I will bring calamity on the men of Anathoth in the year of their reckoning.”

notes.text: Hebrew ʾamen, “surely, so be it,” the response to the covenant curses (Deuteronomy 27:15–26).
The Septuagint lacks verse 7 and most of verse 8, reading only “But they did them not” (Brenton).
Hebrew bosheth, a contemptuous substitute for Baal.
Following the Septuagint, which has “prayers and holy offerings” (Brenton); the Hebrew reads “the many,” which is difficult.
The Hebrew of verses 15–16 is uncertain in places.
Hebrew “with its bread”; the translation follows a slight change of the text, or else read “its fruit.”
Hebrew “kidneys,” regarded as the seat of the emotions.

verses.text:
Righteous are you, Yahweh,
when I bring a case before you;
yet I would argue my cause with you:
Why does the path of the wicked prosper?
Why do all the treacherous live at ease?

You plant them, and they take root;
they grow and bear fruit.
Near are you in their mouth,
but far from their inmost parts.

But you, Yahweh, know me;
you see me and test my heart toward you.
Drag them off like sheep for slaughter,
and set them apart for the day of killing.

Till when shall the earth lie mourning,
the herbage of the countryside dried up?
For the wickedness of its dwellers
beast and bird have perished,
for they said, “He will not see what becomes of us.”

For even your brothers and your father’s house,
even they have dealt treacherously with you;
even they shout loudly after you.
Do not trust them,
though they speak fair words to you.

It has been turned into a wasteland;
waste and mourning, it lies before me.
All the land is made a waste,
since no one takes it to heart.

Over all the bare heights in the wilderness
destroyers have come,
for the sword of Yahweh devours
from one end of the land to the other;
no flesh has peace.

Wheat they sowed, but thorns they reaped;
they have worn themselves out to no profit.
Be ashamed{d} of your harvests
because of the fierce anger of Yahweh.”

This is what Yahweh says concerning all my evil neighbors who touch the heritage I gave my people Israel to possess: “See, I am uprooting them from their land, and the house of Judah I will uproot from among them.
And after I have uprooted them, I will again have compassion on them, and bring them back, each to his heritage and each to his land.
And if they will diligently learn the ways of my people, to swear by my name, ‘As Yahweh lives,’ even as they taught my people to swear by Baal, then they shall be built up in the midst of my people.
But if any nation will not listen, then I will pluck up that nation, plucking it up and destroying it,” declares Yahweh.

notes.text: Or “if only in a peaceful land you feel secure.”
Hebrew “the pride of the Jordan,” the dense growth along the river, home of lions (49:19).
The Hebrew is uncertain; the Septuagint reads, “Is not my inheritance to me a hyena’s cave?” (Brenton, modernized).
Or, with a change of vowels, “They shall be ashamed.”

verses.text: This is what Yahweh said to me: “Go and buy yourself a linen waistcloth{a} and wrap it about your loins, but do not let it get into water.”
So I bought a waistcloth as Yahweh directed and wrapped it about my loins.
Then Yahweh’s word came to me a second time:
“Take the waistcloth you bought, the one about your loins, and set out for Perath;{b} hide it there in a cleft of the rock.”
So I went and hid it at Perath, as Yahweh had ordered me.
After many days Yahweh said to me, “Set out for Perath, and retrieve from there the waistcloth I ordered you to hide there.”
So I went to Perath, dug, and took the waistcloth from the place where I had hidden it. And look—the waistcloth was rotted, fit for nothing at all.
Then Yahweh’s word came to me:
“This is what Yahweh says: Just so will I rot the pride of Judah and the great pride of Jerusalem.
This evil people, who refuse to hear my words, who walk in their own obstinate hearts and go after other gods to serve them and bow to them, shall be like this waistcloth, fit for nothing at all.

For just as a waistcloth hugs a man’s waist, so I bound to myself all Israel’s house and all Judah’s house,” declares Yahweh, “to be my people, my renown, my praise, and my honor; yet they refused to listen.

“Speak to them also this word: ‘This is what Yahweh, Israel’s God, says: Every jar is to be filled with wine.’ And when they answer you, ‘Do we not know perfectly well that every jar is to be filled with wine?’

then say to them, ‘This is what Yahweh says: Look, I am about to fill with drunkenness all who live in this land—the kings who sit for David on his throne, the priests, the prophets, and all Jerusalem’s residents.
And I will smash them one against another, fathers and sons alike,’ declares Yahweh. ‘I will show no pity, nor spare, nor have compassion, so as not to destroy them.’”

Listen and give ear; be not proud,
for Yahweh has spoken.

Give glory to Yahweh your God
before he brings darkness,
before your feet stumble
on the twilight mountains,
and while you wait for light
he turns it into the shadow of death
and makes it deep gloom.

But if you will not hear,
my soul will weep in secret for your pride;
my eye will weep bitterly and run down with tears,
because Yahweh’s flock has been taken captive.

Say to the king and to the queen mother:{c}
“Sit down low,
for your splendid crown
has come down from your heads.”

The towns of the Negev{d} are shut up,
with none to open them;
all Judah is carried into exile,
wholly carried into exile.

Lift up your eyes and see
those coming from the north.
Where is the flock that was given you,
your beautiful flock?

What will you say when he sets over you as head
those whom you yourself taught
to be your intimate friends?{e}
Will not pangs take hold of you
like a woman in childbirth?

And if you say in your heart,
“Why have these things come upon me?”—
for the greatness of your iniquity
your skirts are lifted up
and your heels suffer violence.{f}

Can the Cushite{g} change his skin,
or the leopard his spots?
Then you also can do good,
you who are schooled in evil.

I will scatter them like chaff
driven by the wind of the desert.

This is your lot,
the portion I have measured out to you, declares Yahweh,
because you have forgotten me
and trusted in falsehood.

I myself will strip up your skirts over your face,
and your shame will be seen.

Your adulteries and your neighings,
your lewd harlotry
on the hills in the field—
I have seen your detestable things.
Woe to you, O Jerusalem!
How long will you remain unclean?

notes.text: Hebrew ʾezor, a garment worn next to the body, perhaps a loincloth or sash.

Hebrew Perath is the usual name of the Euphrates, about 350 miles (560 kilometers) away, and the Septuagint reads “the Euphrates” (Brenton). Some interpreters think of Parah (Joshua 18:23), a village about 4 miles (6 kilometers) from Anathoth.
Hebrew gevirah, “great lady,” the king’s mother, who held an official position; probably Nehushta, mother of Jehoiachin (2 Kings 24:8).
Negev, “dry land,” the arid south of Judah.
The Hebrew of this verse is uncertain.
A euphemism for sexual violation.
Cushite, a man from Cush (the upper Nile region, modern Sudan), known for dark skin.

verses.text: The word of Yahweh that came to Jeremiah concerning the drought:{a}

“Judah mourns,
and her gates languish;
her people lie in black upon the ground,
and the cry of Jerusalem goes up.

Since the soil is shattered,
since no rain has fallen on the land,
the farmers are dismayed;
they muffle their heads.

Even the doe in the field
gives birth and forsakes her fawn,
because there is no grass.

O Hope of Israel,
its Savior in time of trouble,
why should you be like a sojourner in the land,
like a traveler who turns aside to lodge for a night?

Why should you be like a man dumbfounded,
like a mighty man who cannot save?
Yet you, O Yahweh, are in our midst,
and we are called by your name;
do not leave us.”
Yahweh said to me, “Do not pray for this people’s welfare.
Though they fast, I will not hear their cry; and though they offer burnt offering and grain offering, I will not accept them; but by the sword, by famine, and by pestilence I will consume them.”
Then I said, “Ah, Lord Yahweh! Look, the prophets keep telling them, ‘You shall not see the sword, nor shall famine come upon you; I will give you lasting peace in this place.’”

And Yahweh said to me, “Falsehood the prophets prophesy in my name. I did not send them, nor command them, nor speak to them. A lying vision, worthless divination, and the deceit of their own minds{b} they prophesy to you.

So this is what Yahweh says about the prophets who prophesy in my name though I never sent them, and who keep saying, ‘No sword or famine will touch this land’: By sword and by famine those very prophets will be finished off.

And the people to whom they prophesy shall be cast out into Jerusalem’s streets, victims of famine and sword, with none to bury them—them, their wives, their sons, and their daughters. For I will pour out their evil upon them.

“You shall say to them this word:
‘Let my eyes run down with tears night and day,
and let them not cease,
for with a great wound the virgin daughter of my people is broken,
with a very grievous blow.

If I go out into the field,
look—those slain by the sword!
And if I enter the city,
look—the diseases of famine!
For both prophet and priest roam about in a land they know not.’”{c}

Have you cast Judah off completely?
Is Zion abhorrent to your soul?
Why have you smitten us
past all mending?
We hoped for peace, and nothing good arrived;
for a season of healing, and see—panic.

We acknowledge, O Yahweh, our wickedness,
the iniquity of our fathers,
for we have sinned against you.

Are there any among the empty idols of the nations that can bring rain?
Or can the heavens give showers?
Is it not you, O Yahweh our God?
So we hope in you,
for you do all these things.

notes.text: Hebrew batstsaroth, “the times of dearth” or “the droughts.”
Hebrew “heart.”
Or “go off trading in a land they do not know”; the Hebrew is uncertain.

verses.text: Then Yahweh said to me, “Even if Moses and Samuel stood before me, my soul would not turn toward this people. Send them from my presence; let them be gone!
I will appoint over them four kinds of destroyers,” declares Yahweh: “the sword to slay, the dogs to drag away, and the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth to devour and to destroy.
I will turn them into an object of dread for every realm on earth, on account of what Manasseh{a} son of Hezekiah, Judah’s king, committed in Jerusalem.

“For who will take pity on you, Jerusalem?
Who will lament over you?
Who will step aside
to inquire how you fare?

Woe is me, my mother, that you bore me,
a man of strife and a man of contention to all the land!
I have not lent, nor have men lent to me,
yet every one of them curses me.

Can one break iron,
iron from the north, and bronze?{c}

Your riches and your stores I will hand over as spoil, at no cost,
for all your sins, in every part of your land.

I will make you slaves to your foes{d}
in a country unknown to you,
for my anger has lit a fire
that will blaze against you.”

Your words were found, and I ate them,
and your word became to me a joy
and the delight of my heart,
for I am called by your name,
O Yahweh, God of Armies.

Never did I sit among the revelers
or make merry with them;
under your hand I sat by myself,
for you had filled me with fury.

Why has my agony no end,
my wound no cure, past all healing?
Will you indeed prove to me a treacherous wadi,
a stream whose waters cannot be relied on?

So Yahweh replied:
“If you turn back, I will take you back,
and you will stand in my service.
If you separate the precious from the worthless,
you will be like my own mouth.
Let them come round to you,
but you must not go over to them.

And to this people I will make you
a fortified wall of bronze;
they will fight against you,
but they shall not prevail over you,
for I am with you
to save you and deliver you, declares Yahweh.

I will rescue you out of the power of evildoers,
and ransom you from the clutch of tyrants.”

notes.text: Manasseh reigned about 697–642 B.C.; his sins are recounted in 2 Kings 21:1–18 and 23:26–27.
The Hebrew of verses 11–12 is difficult; the Septuagint differs considerably, reading, “So be it, Lord, in their prosperity” (Brenton). Some ancient witnesses read the verse as Jeremiah’s words.
Or “Can iron and bronze break iron from the north?”
So many Hebrew manuscripts, the Septuagint, and Syriac (compare 17:4); the standard Hebrew text reads “I will make them pass over with your enemies.”

verses.text: Yahweh’s word came to me once more:
“Take no wife for yourself, and father no sons or daughters in this place.
For here is Yahweh’s word concerning the boys and girls born in this place, and concerning the women who give them birth and the men who father them in this land:

They will perish of deadly diseases. None will mourn them, none will bury them; they will lie like manure on the face of the soil. By sword and by famine they will be finished off, and their carcasses will feed the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth.

“For so says Yahweh: Enter no house of the mourning banquet;{a} go not in to lament or to show sympathy, for from this people I have taken away my peace,” declares Yahweh, “my steadfast love and my tender mercies.{b}
Great and small alike will perish in this land. They will go unburied; no one will mourn for them, nor gash himself, nor shave his head on their account.
No one will break bread for the mourner to console him for the dead, nor will anyone hand him the cup of consolation for his father or his mother.
Into a house of feasting likewise you must not go, to sit down with them to eat and drink.

For this is what Yahweh of Armies, Israel’s God, says: Look, before your eyes and in your days I am silencing in this place the sound of merriment and the sound of joy, the voice of bridegroom and the voice of bride.

“And when you report all these words to this people and they ask you, ‘On what grounds has Yahweh decreed all this great calamity against us? What is our guilt? What sin have we committed against Yahweh our God?’
then answer them, ‘It is because your fathers abandoned me,’ declares Yahweh, ‘and went after other gods, serving them and bowing down to them. Me they abandoned, and my law they did not keep.
And you have done worse than your fathers, for look, each of you walks in the obstinacy of his evil heart, refusing to listen to me.
So I will hurl you out of this land into a land that neither you nor your fathers have known, and there you will serve other gods day and night, for I will show you no favor.’
“Yet look, days are coming,” declares Yahweh, “when it will no longer be said, ‘By the life of Yahweh, who brought the sons of Israel up from Egypt,’

but instead, ‘By the life of Yahweh, who led Israel’s sons up out of the north country and out of every land to which he had scattered them.’ For back to their own soil I will restore them, the soil I bestowed on their ancestors.

“Look, I am sending for many fishermen,” declares Yahweh, “and they will fish them out. Afterward I will send for many hunters, and they will hunt them down on every mountain and every hill and out of the clefts of the rocks.
For my eyes are on all their ways; they are not concealed from my face, nor is their guilt hidden from my eyes.
First{c} I will repay double for their guilt and their sin, because they have polluted my land with the carcasses of their detestable idols and filled my heritage with their abominations.”

Yahweh, my might and my fortress,
my shelter when trouble comes,
from earth’s farthest reaches
the nations will come to you, saying:
“Our fathers owned nothing but a lie,
a puff of air, useless through and through.

Can a man make gods for himself?
Such are no gods!”

“Therefore, look, I will make them know—
this once I will make them know
my hand and my might,
and they will know that my name is Yahweh.”

notes.text: Hebrew marzeaḥ, a ritual banquet, here held for mourning.
The Septuagint lacks “my steadfast love and my compassion” and the first half of verse 6 (Brenton).
The Septuagint lacks “First” (Brenton).

verses.text:
while their sons remember their altars
and their Asherah poles{c}
beside every leafy tree
on the high hills,

O my mountain set in the countryside!
Your riches and every treasure of yours I will hand over as spoil,
your shrines too, for the sin in every part of your land.

Through your own fault you will lose hold
of the inheritance I bestowed on you,
and I will make you slaves to your foes
in a country strange to you,
for you have lit a fire in my nostrils
that will blaze for all time.”

This is what Yahweh says:
“Cursed is the man who relies on mortal man
and makes flesh the arm he leans on,
while his heart veers away from Yahweh.

He will be like a juniper{d} in the Arabah;
he will not see when good arrives,
but will settle in the scorched places of the wilderness,
a salt land where no one lives.

“Blessed is the man who relies on Yahweh,
whose confidence Yahweh is.

“I, Yahweh, probe the heart
and examine the inmost parts,
to repay each man according to his ways,
according to the fruit of his deeds.”

Like a partridge that hatches eggs it did not lay
is the man who gets riches unjustly;
in the middle of his days they will abandon him,
and at his end he will prove a fool.

A throne of glory, set on high from the beginning,
is the place of our sanctuary.

Look, they keep saying to me,
“Where is Yahweh’s word?
Let it come, then!”

Do not become a terror to me;
you are my refuge in the day of calamity.
This is what Yahweh said to me: “Go and stand in the People’s Gate,{h} by which Judah’s kings come in and go out, and in all the gates of Jerusalem,
and say to them, ‘Hear the word of Yahweh, you kings of Judah, and all Judah, and all Jerusalem’s residents who come in by these gates.
This is what Yahweh says: Guard yourselves, as you value your lives, and carry no load on the Sabbath day, nor bring it in through Jerusalem’s gates.
Carry no load out of your houses on the Sabbath day, and do no work at all, but keep the Sabbath day holy, as I commanded your fathers.
Yet they would not listen or turn their ear, but stiffened their necks so as not to hear or take correction.
But if you diligently heed me, declares Yahweh, and carry no burden in by this city’s gates on the Sabbath, but treat the Sabbath as holy by doing no labor on it,

then through the gates of this city will enter kings and princes who sit on David’s throne, riding in chariots and on horses, they and their princes, Judah’s men and Jerusalem’s residents; and this city will be inhabited forever.

And people will come from the towns of Judah and the places around Jerusalem, from the land of Benjamin, from the Shephelah,{i} from the hill country, and from the Negev, bringing burnt offerings and sacrifices, grain offerings and frankincense, and bringing thank offerings to Yahweh’s house.

But if you will not listen to me, to keep the Sabbath day holy and not to carry a load as you enter Jerusalem’s gates on the Sabbath day, then I will kindle a fire in its gates, and it will consume the palaces of Jerusalem and will not be quenched.’”

notes.text: Hebrew shamir, a very hard stone, perhaps emery or diamond.
The Septuagint lacks verses 1–4 (Brenton). Verses 3–4 partly repeat 15:13–14.
Asherah, a Canaanite goddess; her symbol was a wooden pole or stylized tree.
Hebrew ʿarʿar, a desert shrub, perhaps the juniper or a dwarf tamarisk; the Septuagint has “wild tamarisk” (Brenton).

Hebrew ʿaqov, “crooked, deceitful,” recalling the name Jacob. The Septuagint reads, “The heart is deep beyond all things, and it is the man” (Brenton), reflecting Hebrew ʿamoq, “deep,” and ʾenosh, “man,” for ʾanush, “sick.”
Hebrew “from me.”
Or, with a slight change, “I have not run away from being a shepherd after you”; the Hebrew is uncertain.
Or “the Gate of the Sons of the People”; its location is unknown.
Shephelah, “lowland,” the foothills between Judah’s hill country and the coastal plain.

verses.text: The word that came to Jeremiah from Yahweh:
“Get up and go down to the potter’s house, and there I will let you hear my words.”
So I went down to the potter’s workshop, and look—he was at work on the double wheel.{a}
Whenever the vessel he was shaping from the clay was spoiled in the potter’s hand, he would rework it into another vessel, as seemed right to the potter to make.
Then Yahweh’s word came to me:
“House of Israel, can I not deal with you as this potter does?” declares Yahweh. “Look, as clay in the potter’s hand, so are you in my hand, O house of Israel.
At one moment I may speak of a nation or a kingdom, to uproot and pull down and destroy it;
but if that nation I spoke of turns from its evil, I relent of the calamity I planned to bring on it.
At another moment I may speak of a nation or a kingdom, to build and to plant it;
yet should it do what is evil before me, refusing to heed my voice, I will think better of the good I had said I would do for it.

Now therefore, speak to Judah’s men and Jerusalem’s residents: ‘This is what Yahweh says: Look, I am shaping calamity against you and devising a plan against you. Turn back, each of you, from his evil way, and reform your ways and your deeds.’
But they will answer, ‘No use! Our own schemes we will pursue; each of us will do as his stubborn, evil heart dictates.’

“Therefore this is what Yahweh says:
Ask among the nations:
who ever heard the like of this?
A thing most horrible
has the virgin Israel done.

to turn their country into an appalling waste,
an object of perpetual whistling;
all who travel past it shudder
and wag their heads.

Like the east wind I will scatter them
before the enemy;
my back, not my face,{d} I will show them
in the day of their calamity.”

Then they said, “Come, let us devise plans against Jeremiah, for instruction will not perish from the priest, nor counsel from the wise, nor the word from the prophet. Come, let us strike him with the tongue, and let us pay no heed to any of his words.”

Give heed to me, O Yahweh,
and listen to the voice of my adversaries.

Should good be repaid with evil?
Yet they have dug a pit for my life.
Remember how I stood before you
to speak good on their behalf,
to turn your wrath away from them.

Let a cry be heard from their houses,
when you bring raiders on them suddenly,
for they have dug a pit to seize me
and hidden snares for my feet.

Yet you, Yahweh, know
all their plotting against me to kill me.
Do not cover over their iniquity,
nor blot out their sin from before you.
Let them be overthrown before you;
deal with them in the time of your anger.

notes.text: Hebrew “the two stones,” the upper and lower wheels of the potter’s wheel, turned by the feet.
The Hebrew of this line is uncertain; perhaps “the rock of Sirion,” another name for Hermon.
Or “Are the foreign, cold, flowing waters ever plucked up?”; the Hebrew is difficult.
So the Hebrew consonants, read with different vowels; some ancient witnesses read “I will look on their back, not their face.”

verses.text: This is what Yahweh said: “Go and buy a potter’s earthenware jar,{a} and take with you some of the elders of the people and of the senior priests,
and go out to the Valley of Ben-hinnom at the entry of the Potsherd Gate,{b} and proclaim there the words I tell you.

Declare, ‘Listen to Yahweh’s word, O kings of Judah and you who live in Jerusalem. So says Yahweh of Armies, God of Israel: I am about to bring on this place a disaster so great that whoever hears of it, both his ears will ring.

For they have abandoned me and made this place alien, burning offerings in it to other gods whom neither they nor their fathers nor Judah’s kings had known; and they have filled this place with the blood of innocents,
and have built the high places of Baal to burn their sons in the fire as burnt offerings to Baal—a thing I never commanded or spoke of, nor did it enter my mind.
So, mark it, the days are approaching, declares Yahweh, when no longer will this place be named Topheth or Ben-hinnom’s Valley, but Slaughter Valley.

Here in this place I will drain away{c} the counsel of Judah and Jerusalem; I will cause them to fall by the sword before their foes, by the hand of those hunting for their lives, and I will hand over their corpses to be eaten by the birds of the sky and the wild animals of the earth.
I will make this city a horror and a thing to hiss at; everyone who passes by it will be appalled and hiss because of all its wounds.

And I will make them eat the flesh of their sons and the flesh of their daughters, and each will eat the flesh of his neighbor, in the siege and in the distress with which their enemies and those who seek their life will press them.’
“Then you shall break the jar before the eyes of the men who go with you,

and say to them, ‘This is what Yahweh of Armies says: Just so will I break this people and this city, as one breaks a potter’s vessel so that it can never be mended again. And they shall bury in Topheth until there is no place left to bury.
This is what I will do to this place, declares Yahweh, and to its inhabitants, making this city like Topheth.

The houses of Jerusalem and the houses of Judah’s kings shall be defiled like the place of Topheth—all the houses on whose roofs they burned offerings to all the host of the heavens and poured out drink offerings to other gods.’”
Then Jeremiah came from Topheth, where Yahweh had sent him to prophesy, and he stood in the court of Yahweh’s house and said to all the people:

“So says Yahweh of Armies, God of Israel: Mark this—upon this city and all its villages I am bringing every disaster I have decreed against it, because they made their necks rigid and would not hear my words.”

notes.text: Hebrew baqbuq, a narrow-necked flask; the name imitates the gurgling sound of pouring. Its sound anticipates the verb baqqothi, “I will empty out,” in verse 7.
Hebrew Harsith, perhaps the gate where broken pottery was discarded.
Hebrew baqqothi, a play on baqbuq, “jar” (verse 1).

verses.text: Now Pashhur son of Immer, the priest, who was chief officer in Yahweh’s house, heard Jeremiah prophesying these things.
Then Pashhur struck Jeremiah the prophet and put him in the stocks{a} at the Upper Gate of Benjamin, in Yahweh’s house.
On the following day Pashhur let Jeremiah out of the stocks, and Jeremiah told him, “Yahweh’s name for you is not Pashhur, but Magor-missabib.{b}

For this is what Yahweh says: Look, I will make you a terror to yourself and to all your friends. They will fall by the sword of their enemies while your eyes look on. And all Judah I will give into the hand of the king of Babylon; he will carry them captive to Babylon and strike them down with the sword.
All this city’s riches, all its earnings, all its valuables, and every treasure of Judah’s kings I will hand over to their foes, who will loot them, carry them off, and take them away to Babylon.
As for you, Pashhur, you and all your household will go away as captives. To Babylon you will come; there you will die and there be buried, you and every friend of yours to whom you prophesied lies.”

For whenever I speak, I cry out;
“Violence and ruin!” I shout.
For the word of Yahweh has become for me
a reproach and derision all day long.

Yet if I resolve, “I will not bring him to mind
or speak again in his name,”
it turns within my heart into a blazing fire
locked up in my bones;
I am worn out trying to contain it,
and I am not able.

For I hear many muttering,
“Terror all around!
Report him! Yes, let us report him!”
All who were at peace with me
wait for me to trip:
“Maybe he can be lured;
then we will get the better of him
and have our revenge.”

O Yahweh of Armies, who test the righteous,
who see the inmost parts and the heart,
let me see your vengeance upon them,
for to you I have laid bare my cause.

Sing to Yahweh;
praise Yahweh!
For he has rescued the life of the needy
from the hand of evildoers.

A curse on the day
I came to birth!
The day my mother brought me forth—
may no blessing rest on it!

A curse on the man who carried word to my father,
“You have a son, a boy!”
and filled him with gladness.

Let that man be like the cities
that Yahweh overthrew without relenting;
let him hear a cry in the morning
and an alarm at noon,

because he did not slay me before birth,
that my mother might have been my tomb,
her womb pregnant for all time.

Why ever did I leave the womb
to look on trouble and grief,
and finish my days in disgrace?

notes.text: Hebrew mahpeketh, perhaps a device that held the body in a twisted posture.
Magor-missabib, “terror on every side.” The Septuagint reads “Exile” (Brenton) in place of the Hebrew name.
Or “You deceived me, and I was deceived”; the verb pathah is used of seducing (Exodus 22:16).
